title: Inside Bollywood Producer Jackky Bhagnani's Wholesome Weekly Meal Plan
excerpt: From neer dosa with chicken curry to yakhani pulao with raita, the producer shows that eating healthy doesn't have to mean eating boring.
body:
• Bollywood producer Jackky Bhagnani shared his weekly meal plan on Instagram, featuring dishes from stuffed chicken with pesto to yakhani pulao with raita.
  • The spread highlights India's regional culinary diversity, spanning South Indian neer dosa, Mughlai-style yakhani pulao, and protein-rich paneer sizzlers.
  • Bhagnani captioned the post: "Good nutrition is all about balance, nourishment and consistency."
  • The producer and wife Rakul Preet Singh are known for preferring healthier twists on Indian classics at home.

A Week of Regional Indian Dishes

Bollywood producer Jackky Bhagnani offered a window into his daily meals this week with an Instagram post that doubled as a tour of Indian regional cooking. The spread featured six plated meals, each balancing protein, vegetables, and flavour without veering into excess.

The week opened with a stuffed chicken platter served with pesto sauce and sautéed vegetables. A paneer sizzler followed — a spiced slab of paneer coated in a flavourful sauce, paired with sautéed vegetables for fibre. A third meal featured another chicken preparation with vegetables, keeping the protein-forward theme consistent.

South Indian Staples Meet Mughlai Comfort Food

The standout dishes came from opposite ends of India's culinary map. One plate featured neer dosa — the delicate, lace-thin rice crepe from coastal Karnataka — paired with chicken curry and sabzi. Another showcased yakhani pulao, a fragrant Mughlai rice dish cooked with whole spices in a meat-based stock, served alongside a bowl of raita.

The final meal brought together dosa with chicken porial, a South Indian dry stir-fry of bite-sized chicken pieces with onions and traditional spices. It is a pairing familiar to anyone who grew up with Tamil Nadu's everyday cooking.

"Good nutrition is all about balance, nourishment and consistency. Here's a look at the wholesome meals that make up a week."

— Jackky Bhagnani

A Known Food Enthusiast

Bhagnani's passion for food, particularly South Indian cooking, is well documented. In a previous Instagram video, the producer made dosa from scratch — mixing the batter, preparing an aloo sabji filling, spreading it thin on a heated pan, and finishing with ghee, shredded cheese, and a drizzle of chilli sauce. His wife, actress Rakul Preet Singh, has noted that he makes "amazing dosas, and not just plain ones — there's variety, like schezwan dosa."

The skill traces back years. In an interview with Curly Tales, Bhagnani recalled learning the craft from observing a street-side dosa vendor named Mani near his childhood home in Bandra, Mumbai, for four to six years. "Even if I had three dosas, with chutney and all, it would cost me around 110-120 rupees. I was sorted!" he said.

Healthy Twists on Indian Classics

At home, Bhagnani and Rakul Preet Singh favour lighter versions of traditional dishes. Their kitchen has served no-butter butter chicken made with minimal oil and aromatics, paneer substituted for malai in methi matar malai for added protein, and koki made with jowar flour. The approach reflects a broader shift among health-conscious Indians who want traditional flavours without the caloric load.

What Stands Out

The week's meals are notable less for any single dish than for their variety. Stuffed chicken with pesto sits alongside yakhani pulao. Neer dosa shares the rotation with paneer sizzlers. For anyone trying to eat well without giving up regional Indian flavours, Bhagnani's mix-and-match approach — drawing from South Indian, Mughlai, and pan-Indian cooking — offers a workable daily template.
